rules.sourceContent: Technical DebtREQUIRED FOR ARB-2This section lists deliberate design compromises, deviations from target architecture, or sub-optimal choices that are being accepted.For ARB, technical debt is not automatically a problem. Hidden technical debt is the problem.The board needs to understand the impact, why it exists, what the mitigation plan is, and whoowns it.Example: If you are building an integration connecting to mainframe.Data SecurityREQUIRED FOR ARB-2This section explains the security controls protecting the solutionʼs data, including data at rest,data in transit, and authentication and authorization controls. Typically, this is the completedSAINT documentation from Security.For ARB, this helps validate that the design has appropriate security architecture and that dataprotection has been considered as part of the solution, not added later.IntegrationsREQUIRED FOR ARB-2This section describes data flows and integrations, including integration platforms, connectionpoints, and naming where applicable. For ARB, this clarifies how systems exchange data, where integration complexity exists, andwhether the project is using supported integration patterns and platforms.If you have any integrations, they should be documented in detail. What good looks likeA comprehensive list of integrations needed for the solution with the following details:Integration name (e.g. IA-123)Source / Target Name (e.g. PMM to Azure Storage)Integration Type / Schedule (e.g. Batch File @ 10am ET Daily)Tool use (e.g. AZCopy, DataStage, A2A FTP)38

rules.sourceContent: Infrastructure ArchitectureREQUIRED FOR ARB-2This section is to be completed by the Solution Architect. It documents the physical andnetwork infrastructure supporting the solution.Key content includes:Network & Physical Design: a diagram of networking and physical components perenvironment, including all on-premise and/or cloud infrastructure involved in the solution. New Modules Required: a list of new IaC (Infrastructure as Code) modules required for thesolution, if applicable.For ARB, this section answers: Is the infrastructure design sound, appropriately scoped perenvironment, and aligned to enterprise hosting and network standards?Security ArchitectureREQUIRED FOR ARB-2This section is to be completed by the Security Architect. It provides the formal securityassessment, gap analysis, and recommended controls for the solution, aligned with CanadianTire's internal security standards, NIST CSF v2.0, PCI DSS (where applicable), and threatmodelling practices.Key content includes:Scope: which solution components are in scope for the security assessment.Security Assumptions & Constraints: documented assumptions and constraints affectingthe security design.Security Design: a high-level visual representation illustrating trust zones, boundaries,enforcement controls, integrations, and data flows.What good looks likeAn infrastructure diagram showing:Network layers, names, and boundariesService names and connectivityPlatform names and connectivityDatabase names, types, and connectivityStorage names, types, and connectivityIntegration names and transport types39
